question: does every Mermaid block in docs/workflow.md parse, render, and land narrow enough to be readable at GitHub's content width
why_a_render_and_not_a_parse: all 10 blocks parsed AND rendered without error at a point when section 1 was 3141 px wide with a decision subtree flung outside its subgraph. Parsing proves the syntax; only the pixels prove the chart. This file records the pixels.
renderer: mermaid@11 ESM from cdn.jsdelivr.net, theme neutral, mermaid.parse() then mermaid.render() per block
browser: Chromium via Playwright, viewport 1620x1000, devicePixelRatio 1 (scale: css)
measured_from: the rendered SVG's own viewBox, plus getBBox() on every edge path
ceiling_rationale: GitHub's file-view content column is about 880 px. A diagram wider than that is scaled down, and the scale applies to the label text: at 3141 px the 14 px labels render at about 4 px. 1500 px scales to about 0.59x, which keeps a 14 px label above 8 px. Height is not capped, because GitHub scrolls vertically and does not scale for height.
tallest_edge_is_recorded_not_gated: tallest_edge_frac_of_canvas is recorded, NOT a pass criterion. A shared early-exit terminal (block 8's REFUSED, block 7's stop transitions) legitimately produces a full-height edge. What made the first draft unreadable was an edge whose two ends had nothing to do with each other (microphone to ws_gateway, spanning 100% of a 3847 px canvas) combined with the width. Gating on this number would forbid correct charts and would not have caught the actual defect, which width does.
